newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher, spot Nov expires.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher, spot Nov expires.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher across the board on Tuesday, due to the Chicago corn market's overnight price rally and the higher-than-expected expiry price for the spot November contract, traders said.
Prices were 310 to 580 yen higher, with benchmark September up 340 yen at 15,040 yen per tonne.
Buying orders from local investors supported the market from the opening, as the Chicago market's overnight price gains fostered a bullish mood here, the traders said.
The spot November contract expired at 16,340 yen with 60 deliveries.
"Investors saw active selling at the spot month's expiry. But buying emerged in the afternoon after the spot expired higher than expected," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.86-3/4 per bushel at 0815 GMT, compared with $2.86-1/2 on Monday.
The spot November CBOT soybean futures contract was at $6.91 at 0815 GMT, up from $6.88-1/2 at Monday's close.
